interpretations.decision: Generic OIDC JWT access tokens (RFC 9068 shape) verified offline with the locked pyjwt 2.15.1 against an operator-pinned JWKS file (PyJWKSet.from_dict, never PyJWKClient). kid is required and in the set; the algorithm allow-list is RS256/PS256/ES256/EdDSA matched to the key type; exp, iss, aud and sub are required, nbf is honoured and leeway is at most 60 s; aud contains the per-route resource URL resource_base_url/<id> (RFC 8707); the token is at most 8 KiB, checked before decode; principal = (iss, sub). The verifier conforms to the SDK TokenVerifier protocol and is called from the Atlas router with closed fixed-text rejections. RFC 9728 metadata is served unauthenticated for any label-valid id (no enumeration)

An operator-declared set of repositories (closed shared-config JSON), each served on /mcp/<repo_id> with its own derived Config, server state and S39 build_app behind one loopback listener and one shared in-flight gate. The operator policy file maps (issuer, subject) to repository ids and shareable tools; it is the authorization source of truth, reloaded at most once per interval, failing closed to deny-all. Token scopes only narrow (required_scope). Unknown and unauthorized repositories get the same 403; absent or invalid credentials get 401 with WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata

The router rejects 401/403 from the ASGI scope before any body read (withheld-body responses and a receive counter prove it), so no lease, CodeGraph construction, traversal, retrieval or source read happens. A retrieve/context repository argument naming another repository is denied by the handler guard before any lease

The only evidence-bearing store is LeaseRegistry._leases. ScopedLeaseRegistry.scope() = digest({base, authz scope identity}), where the scope identity is sha256 of {principal, repository_id, grant_digest, policy_epoch}, read from a ContextVar set by the guard and failing closed when unset. It is bound into reservations, the token authority, install, authenticate and paging query_digest without changing the token key set. Another principal's cursor or resource gives SCOPE_MISMATCH; another repository's gives INVALID_REFERENCE. Any policy change increments the epoch, so old cursors never revive, and purge_revoked() closes stale leases. No result cache exists and none is added

The only served expansion is graph_query op=impact's before-repository, which is registered as its own repository id (before_repo_id). Impact requires a graph_query grant on every hop via authorize_path; otherwise it is denied before any lease on either repository. S30 cross_repo/* stays offline and unserved; a pure authorize_path test is driven by an S30 world's repository ids

decide() is a pure function of (credential, immutable policy snapshot (policy digest, registry digest, epoch), repository_id, classified request). Its canonical Decision digest is identical across repeats, shuffled policy order and a fresh interpreter

test_dry_run and memex_read are never grantable or callable in shared mode (policy loader, guard and SharedEnforcement), and shared Configs force test_execution_enabled=False with a refusal when the environment enables it. Every other tool requires a per-repository grant, checked by the guard and re-checked by SharedEnforcement.assert_read_only/assert_rate_limit, the first calls of dispatch and read_resource
